name: vwap_reclaim_trend_001_5s
author: adapted from cursor-fast
thesis: This strategy exploits trend continuation after a temporary VWAP dislocation is absorbed and price reclaims the benchmark. The inefficiency exists because many intraday participants use VWAP as a risk-transfer anchor and re-enter only after confirmation, and it persists because chop regimes create frequent fake reclaims.
mechanism: VWAP is the institutional execution benchmark. When spot deviates significantly from session VWAP, algorithmic execution engines increase order flow to mean-revert their fills toward VWAP. This creates measurable gravitational pull, especially during lower-volume mid-session periods when fewer competing flows are present.

exit.signal_exit: exit when close crosses back through vwap

weaknesses: Performance is regime-dependent and weakens materially when session structure changes mid-trade.
Fast moves can create worse-than-assumed slippage and reduce realized edge versus paper assumptions.
Crowding risk can compress payoff and make execution quality unstable in the most obvious setups.
prior_art: VWAP reclaim continuation with EMA/ADX filter
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
